answer: Each PoA identity locks bonded collateral in an escrow, and cryptographic evidence aggregates related equivocations: for k coordinated identities, the penalty grows as O(k^2), rather than linearly. After detection, control of a sybil swarm triggers an exponential-in-k capital-loss multiplier, including collateral depreciation, so replication is uneconomic. A beacon may wander among velvet aliases, but attribution binds every signature to accountable stake.
